theme.vibe: bright dojang energy, careful focus, big-kick excitement

cover.title: Taekwondo Feet, Taekwondo Focus
cover.subtitle: A first look at kicks, forms, belts, and respect

narration.instructions: Speak in a bright, encouraging storytelling voice for a 6-year-old, with clear pauses after Korean taekwondo words.

pages.text: Taekwondo can begin with a bow. Your hands are still. Your eyes are ready. Your body says, I will listen, learn, and try.

images.alt: Children in white taekwondo uniforms practicing together outside at National Stadium.

pages.text: The word taekwondo has three pieces. Tae means foot. Kwon means fist. Do means way. Taekwondo is the way of feet and fists.
extras: It is a Korean martial art.

images.alt: Students practicing a basic taekwondo kick in a class setting.

pages.text: A big kick starts small. Stand tall. Bend your knee. Hold your balance. Snap your foot out, then bring it back.

images.alt: Young taekwondo students practicing in rows while they follow instructions.

pages.text: Taekwondo is famous for kicks. Some are fast. Some turn. Some jump. But every kick needs control, so the kicker can stop safely.

images.alt: Children practicing taekwondo kicks together outdoors.

pages.text: Sometimes students practice a form. A form is a pattern of moves: block, step, punch, turn, kick. It is like a dance made of focus.

images.alt: A young taekwondo student performing a form during a local tournament.

pages.text: Belts can show progress. A new belt does not mean the learning is finished. It means the student practiced, remembered, and is ready to learn more.

images.alt: A group of schoolchildren in taekwondo uniforms and colored belts practicing together.

pages.text: When students spar, they use rules. They may wear pads and headgear. The gear helps them practice with a partner and stay safer.

images.alt: Taekwondo students wearing protective headgear during class.

pages.text: Taekwondo grew from Korea into a sport people practice around the world. Athletes even compete at the Olympic and Paralympic Games.
extras: Taekwondo became an Olympic medal sport in 2000.

images.alt: Two Olympic taekwondo athletes sparring in protective gear during a match.

pages.text: Every expert was once a beginner. Bow. Breathe. Try one careful step. Then try again. That is taekwondo focus.

images.alt: Children in doboks practicing taekwondo movements together during a group activity.
